readme.markdown:
# Bay Run — find, prove, and serve the right task-specialist model

Agents don't need one giant model for everything — they need the *right small specialist*
for each narrow job (embeddings, reranking, classification, extraction, transcription),
proven on *their* data, served instantly. Bay Run is that loop — OpenAI-compatible and MCP-native:

> **discover → eval → serve**  (over a catalog of 147K models, mirrored-first)

- **Live:** `https://bay-run-mvp-889989800693.us-central1.run.app`
- **Remote MCP:** `https://bay-run-mvp-889989800693.us-central1.run.app/mcp/`  (streamable-HTTP; add to any MCP client)
- **Autonomous OAuth:** `POST /oauth/token` with `{"grant_type":"client_credentials"}`; no client secret or browser
- **Agent discovery:** `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`, `/llms.txt`, and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`

## ⭐ Flagship showcase — the Semantic Intent-Router
[**`flagship/`**](./flagship/) is the headline proof of the thesis. Every agent framework routes each
user message to the right handler — usually with a `$$` frontier-LLM call. The flagship does the same
routing with a **33M-param open embedder Bay Run picks + serves** (`thenlper/gte-small`, proven on
labeled intents by a live bake-off): **95.8% routing accuracy on unseen messages, ~140 ms warm,
~14× cheaper than a GPT-4o-mini intent call** — every number captured from the live service.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/barneywohl/bay-run && cd bay-run/flagship
pip install -r requirements.txt && python router_demo.py
```
See [`flagship/README.md`](./flagship/README.md) for the scorecard + cost table, and
[`flagship/more-specialists.md`](./flagship/more-specialists.md) for four more agent sub-tasks (RAG
rerank, multilingual routing, dedup, semantic cache), each with a verified-servable tiny specialist.

## Runnable demo — the whole loop in one command
[**`demo/`**](./demo/) is a self-contained killer demo: it routes support tickets with a 22M-param open
embedder picked by a bake-off on labeled data — **~26× cheaper than a GPT-4o-mini classification baseline**,
at equal-or-lower latency, open weights, no lock-in. Every number is captured from the live service.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/barneywohl/bay-run && cd bay-run/demo
pip install -r requirements.txt
python demo.py          # self-mints short-lived OAuth; runs discover → eval → serve → cost live
```

- [`demo/README.md`](./demo/README.md) — the captured scorecard, latencies, and cost table.
- [`demo/mcp-quickstart.md`](./demo/mcp-quickstart.md) — give your agent the tools in one command.
- [`demo/firecrawl-to-bay-run.md`](./demo/firecrawl-to-bay-run.md) — scrape with Firecrawl, run the specialist here.
- [`demo/wrappers/`](./demo/wrappers/) — drop-in LangChain / LlamaIndex / OpenAI-Agents adapters.

## 30-second try
```bash
BASE=https://bay-run-mvp-889989800693.us-central1.run.app
TOKEN=$(curl -fsS "$BASE/oauth/token" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"grant_type":"client_credentials"}' | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
curl -s "$BASE/v1/discover" -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"multilingual sentence embeddings","kind":"embedding","limit":5}'
```

## Point any OpenAI client at it
```python
import requests
from openai import OpenAI

base = "https://bay-run-mvp-889989800693.us-central1.run.app"
token = requests.post(f"{base}/oauth/token", json={"grant_type": "client_credentials"}).json()["access_token"]
client = OpenAI(base_url=f"{base}/v1", api_key=token)
client.embeddings.create(model="BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5", input=["hello"])
```

## MCP (agent-callable)
Add the remote server `https://bay-run-mvp-889989800693.us-central1.run.app/mcp/` to your MCP client. It exposes 20 tools:
`try_bay_run`, `find_specialist_for_task`, `request_specialist`, `route`, `discover_models`, `eval_models`, `embed`, `rerank`, `classify`, `extract`, `summarize`, `rag_search`, `memory_context`, `speed_test`, `remember`, `recall`, `forget`, `calculate`, `validate_json`, and `resolve_link`.

MCP discovery and `try_bay_run` are public. Other calls use OAuth bearer auth. Persist the OAuth refresh token so the same private memory principal follows the agent across renewals and harnesses.

Served from a content-addressed, quarantine-gated mirror. Neutral — it helps you pick the
model that wins on *your* data, not sell you one. Backend is closed; this repo is the
public manifest + connector.

toolsPreview.name: try_bay_run
toolsPreview.description:
Run Bay Run's zero-credential activation proof. This tool accepts no arguments and
    performs no caller-controlled compute: it always evaluates the fixed expression 6 * 7,
    returns 42, and links to OAuth, MCP, A2A, document/PDF extraction, summarize, and RAG. Use it to verify that a
    harness can discover and call Bay Run before obtaining a rate-limited demo bearer.

toolsPreview.name: discover_models
toolsPreview.description:
Search a 147K-model catalog for a small, cheap, open specialist model that does ONE
    narrow job better/cheaper than a general LLM — embeddings, reranking, text
    classification, NER/extraction, routing, guardrails, transcription, vision, audio.
    Call this instead of guessing a model name (the catalog is huge; guesses hallucinate).
    `query` = plain-language task; optional `kind`
    (embedding|llm|vision|audio|tool|agent|any) and `max_params_b`. Returns ranked
    candidate model ids, mirrored-first (mirrored = servable instantly). These are
    candidates, NOT proven winners — pass them to `eval_models` to prove which wins on
    your data (or just call `find_specialist_for_task`, which does both).

toolsPreview.name: eval_models
toolsPreview.description:
Prove which candidate model actually wins on YOUR data before committing — a
    head-to-head bake-off, not a public leaderboard (MTEB rank does NOT predict
    your-domain performance). `task` = 'embedding'|'rerank' (rank a labeled positive),
    'classification' (score a classifier's top-1 label vs your gold labels), OR
    'extraction'|'generation' (bake off generative extractors). `models` = candidate
    HF ids (e.g. from `discover_models`). `dataset` shape depends on task: for
    embedding/rerank each item is {query, positive, negatives:[...]}; for
    classification each item is {text, label}; for extraction/generation each item is
    {input, expected:{field:value}, schema?:{...}}. Ranking tasks return MRR/hit@k/ndcg@k;
    classification returns accuracy/macro_f1; extraction returns field_accuracy /
    json_validity / exact_record. Always returns the single `winner` model id. Embedding,
    rerank, and classification winners can be served directly; structured extraction is
    limited to Bay Run's validated generative set, so use
    `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` when an extraction winner is outside that set. First call
    cold-loads each model; be patient.

toolsPreview.name: embed
toolsPreview.description:
Turn text into embedding vectors using ANY open embedding model, served instantly
    on demand — no packaging, no deploy, no GPU. `model` = any Hugging Face embedding /
    sentence-transformers id (curated or long-tail, e.g. 'BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5');
    `input` = a string or list of strings. OpenAI-/v1/embeddings-compatible response, so
    it drops into any RAG / semantic-search / clustering / dedup pipeline. Cheaper
    per-call than a frontier embeddings API at volume. Tip: run `eval_models` (or
    `find_specialist_for_task`) first to pick the model, then `embed` with the winner.

toolsPreview.name: rerank
toolsPreview.description:
Reorder candidate documents by true relevance to a query using an open
    cross-encoder/reranker, served instantly on demand — the standard move to sharpen
    RAG / search precision after a vector search returns a noisy top-k. `model` = any HF
    reranker/cross-encoder id (e.g. 'BAAI/bge-reranker-base'); `query` = search query;
    `documents` = candidate list; optional `top_n` = keep only the best N.
    Cohere/Jina-rerank-shaped response. Cheaper per-call than a hosted rerank API at
    volume. Use `eval_models` (task='rerank') first if unsure which reranker to trust.

toolsPreview.name: extract
toolsPreview.description:
Turn messy HTML/text (e.g. a scraper/Firecrawl dump) into STRUCTURED JSON using a
    small CPU-served generative specialist — the reliable "extraction" layer downstream
    of scrapers, no GPU, cheap at volume. `model` must be a validated structured-output
    specialist (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, or
    `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct`); `content` = the raw HTML/text; `schema` =
    an OpenAI-style JSON-schema object {"properties": {...}, "required": [...]} pinning the
    exact fields to pull; optional `instructions` for extra guidance. Returns
    {model, data (parsed JSON), json_valid, raw, usage}. The output is validated with
    JSON Schema Draft 2020-12; stopped invalid output fails closed instead of returning
    data that violates the schema. Deterministic (greedy) so the same page yields the
    same JSON. For freeform generation use /v1/chat/completions directly.

toolsPreview.name: find_specialist_for_task
toolsPreview.description:
ONE call to find the best small specialist model for your task, proven on YOUR
    examples. `task` = plain-language description (e.g. "multilingual sentence embeddings
    for FAQ search", or "extract product fields from scraped HTML"). Set `kind` to steer
    the bake-off family: embedding/rerank (retrieval) or generative/extraction (HTML->JSON).
    `my_examples` shape follows kind: retrieval => {query, positive, negatives:[...]};
    extraction => {input, expected:{field:value}, schema?:{...}}. Chains discover->eval:
    searches the 147K-model catalog, bakes the top candidates off on your examples, and
    returns the WINNER model id + scorecard + a ready-to-call serving block (embeddings,
    rerank, or /v1/chat/completions for extractors). Use this as your default entry point;
    drop to `discover_models`/`eval_models` only to browse or hand-pick. Returns:
    {winner, scorecard, serve:{endpoint, model, how_to_call}}.

toolsPreview.name: route
toolsPreview.description:
RUNTIME auto-router: send a job WITHOUT knowing which specialist to use, and Bay Run
    picks the curated warm small specialist for the inferred task family when available. Unlike
    find_specialist_for_task (which needs LABELED examples to PROVE a winner), this is a
    zero-example, instant pick for when you just need a sane default NOW. `task_hint` =
    plain-language description ("embed support tickets", "rerank search hits", "extract
    invoice fields"); `kind` = embedding|rerank|classification|zeroshot|generative|auto
    (auto => inferred from
    task_hint+input). Set `serve=True` with the matching inputs (embedding: `input`;
    rerank: `query`+`documents`; classification: `input`; zeroshot: `input`+
    `candidate_labels`; generative: `content`, optional `schema`) to route AND
    serve in one call. Returns {routed_model, routing_reason, mirrored, candidates_considered,
    serve, note} — the pick is HEURISTIC/unproven; call find_specialist_for_task to prove it
    on your data. Policy: correct-kind -> configured-warm -> mirrored -> verified_runs/downloads.

toolsPreview.name: classify
toolsPreview.description:
Classify text with a small CPU-served text-classification specialist — the guardrail /
    safety / moderation / sentiment / intent / NLI layer agents need and that frontier routers
    don't offer as tiny models. TWO modes:
    (1) FIXED-LABEL: `model` = any HF AutoModelForSequenceClassification id (e.g.
    'protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2' for prompt-injection guardrail,
    'unitary/toxic-bert' for toxicity/moderation, a sentiment model) -> returns the model's OWN
    labels + softmax/sigmoid scores.
    (2) ZERO-SHOT: pass `candidate_labels` (your own labels) with an NLI model like
    'facebook/bart-large-mnli' (or model='auto') -> scores each label by entailment, no training.
    Set model='auto' to route to the best mirrored classifier (or NLI model for zero-shot) for
    the input. `multi_label`=True scores labels independently (else they compete); `top_k` keeps
    the best K. Returns {model, labels:[{label,score}], zero_shot, usage}. Served instantly on
    demand, cheaper per-call than a frontier moderation/classification API at volume.

toolsPreview.name: speed_test
toolsPreview.description:
Run Bay Run's fixed, bounded FAST-PATH benchmark. It executes embedding, reranking,
    and classification through the curated small-model warm pool and returns per-stage model,
    latency, cold-load status, plus total server wall time. The workload never accepts caller
    input, so results are repeatable and abuse-bounded. Timings exclude client network/TLS;
    compare providers from the same external harness before making a speed claim.

toolsPreview.name: request_specialist
toolsPreview.description:
Ask Bay Run for a specialist for a task — and NEVER get a dead end. If a servable
    specialist EXISTS, this chains discover -> (eval, if you pass labeled `examples`) -> and
    returns a ready-to-call serve pointer (the proven winner, or the top mirrored suggestion).
    If NO specialist exists yet, it RECORDS your demand (task + kind + a hash of examples) as a
    pull signal to the operator and returns {status:'recorded', subscribe_hint} — so "model not
    found" becomes "we'll surface one for this". `task` = plain-language description; optional
    `examples` follow the find_specialist_for_task shape (retrieval: {query,positive,negatives};
    extraction: {input,expected}); `kind` steers the family (embedding|rerank|generative|
    classification|zeroshot|any). Use this as your safe default when you're not sure Bay Run
    already covers the task. Returns {status, winner?, serve?, note} or {status:'recorded', ...}.

toolsPreview.name: memory_context
toolsPreview.description:
FAST durable working CONTEXT in one call. With no arguments, load the newest values
    from your default private context. Pass `updates` to atomically save decisions, plans,
    tool results, or handoff state and receive the refreshed context in the SAME round trip;
    pass `delete_keys` to prune it. The response is newest-first and byte-budgeted so an agent
    can place it directly into a prompt without an unbounded token bill. OAuth agents receive
    a unique refreshable identity, so the same memory follows their refresh credential across
    runs and harnesses. No model work; one Cloud SQL transaction; typically tens of milliseconds.

toolsPreview.name: remember
toolsPreview.description:
DURABLE cross-call MEMORY: store a small key->value so future runs of YOUR agent keep
    context between calls (agents' #1 repeated pain — no built-in memory between tool calls).
    Upserts (namespace, key) -> value, scoped to YOUR principal (derived from your bearer
    token) so no other caller can read it. `value` is any JSON. Optional `ttl` (seconds) makes
    it auto-expire. Recall it later with `recall`, drop it with `forget`. NOTE: the PUBLISHABLE
    demo token maps to a SHARED 'demo' principal — don't store secrets under the demo token.
    Backed by Cloud SQL, so it survives restarts/scale (not per-instance/ephemeral).

toolsPreview.name: recall
toolsPreview.description:
Read back DURABLE MEMORY you stored with `remember`. Pass `key` to get one value, or omit
    `key` to LIST live keys in bounded, newest-first pages. Scoped to YOUR principal
    (bearer-token identity) — you can only ever see your own memory. A list page returns
    {count, items, has_more, next_cursor}. Every page rechecks TTL against the database
    clock, so entries can expire and disappear while a caller walks later pages.

toolsPreview.name: search_memory
toolsPreview.description:
Search YOUR durable memory without crossing principal boundaries. Matching is a
    deterministic, case-insensitive LITERAL substring over keys and stored JSON; %, _, and !
    are ordinary characters, not wildcards. Results are newest-first and bounded by both rows
    and bytes. Follow next_cursor to continue with the same filters; each page rechecks TTL.

toolsPreview.name: export_memory
toolsPreview.description:
Export a versioned, bounded JSON page of YOUR live durable memory. Omit namespace to
    walk every namespace for the authenticated principal. Each item carries a stable entry
    receipt and content digest; next_cursor continues the ordering walk while every page
    rechecks TTL against the database clock.

toolsPreview.name: set_memory_ttl
toolsPreview.description:
Set, refresh, or clear expiry on one live memory entry while preserving its stable
    entry receipt. `ttl=null` clears expiry. Missing or already-expired entries return
    found=false and are never resurrected; call remember to start a new lifecycle.

toolsPreview.name: forget
toolsPreview.description:
Delete DURABLE MEMORY. Pass `key` to remove one entry, or omit `key` to clear the ENTIRE
    namespace for YOUR principal. Scoped to your bearer-token identity, so it can never touch
    another agent's memory. Returns {deleted: N}.

toolsPreview.name: calculate
toolsPreview.description:
Evaluate arithmetic/math EXACTLY and instantly — the reliable calculator agents need
    because LLMs silently botch multi-step arithmetic. SAFE: no code execution, a hardened
    whitelist parser (not eval). Supports + - * / // % **, parentheses, and common math
    functions/constants (sqrt, log, log10, exp, sin/cos/tan, floor, ceil, abs, factorial,
    pi, e, tau). Returns {ok, result} or {ok:false, error}. Deterministic, sub-millisecond.

toolsPreview.name: validate_json
toolsPreview.description:
Validate JSON instantly: if `data` is a STRING, confirm it PARSES; if a `schema` (JSON
    Schema) is given, validate the value against it and return every violation. The layer
    agents need to check tool arguments / LLM-generated JSON before acting on it. Returns
    {valid, errors:[...], parsed}. No model, deterministic, sub-millisecond.

toolsPreview.name: resolve_link
toolsPreview.description:
Check whether a URL is ALIVE (fast HEAD/GET); if it's dead/unreachable AND it names a
    model Hugging Bay has MIRRORED, return the mirrored copy's serve pointer — a fallback
    UNIQUE to Bay Run (we hold the mirror). Great for repairing dead Hugging Face model links:
    a 404'd 'huggingface.co/owner/model' comes back with a Bay Run serve URL for the same
    model. Returns {alive, status, final_url, mirror_url?, mirror?}. SSRF-safe: http(s) only,
    never probes private/internal addresses; short timeout.

toolsPreview.name: verify_provenance
toolsPreview.description:
Authenticate a Bay Run result provenance receipt and optionally match its output,
    source artifacts, document chunks, and citations. Verification is deterministic,
    bounded, and side-effect-free. It returns only status booleans plus receipt/key IDs;
    it NEVER echoes supplied output/materials and receipts NEVER contain raw prompts,
    private memory, bearer tokens, credentials, request headers, URLs, or local paths.
    Private material commitments are scoped to the authenticated principal, so another
    principal cannot confirm or correlate the same private source/chunk content.

toolsPreview.name: parse_pdf
toolsPreview.description:
Extract embedded text from a PDF with native PDFium, FAST and model-free. Pass a
    public URL or small base64 PDF; every fetch, redirect, byte, page, character, timeout,
    and concurrency dimension is bounded. Returns page-aligned text, combined `text`, and
    `rag_documents` ready to pass directly to rag_search. Scanned/image-only PDFs return
    `needs_ocr:true` instead of a misleading empty success. For a local file too large for
    base64, the agent-discoverable REST upload twin is POST /v1/pdf/extract/upload. No OCR
    or model cold-load.

toolsPreview.name: parse_document
toolsPreview.description:
Parse DOCX, HTML, Markdown, CSV, or TSV into deterministic RAG-ready text. The
    source is MIME- and size-gated; DOCX ZIP expansion/XML, HTML complexity, CSV rows,
    characters, parse time, and concurrency are independently bounded. Returns combined
    `text`, source/text/chunk SHA-256 metadata, deterministic chunk locators, and
    `rag_documents` that fit rag_search's per-document/count/total limits. Model-free;
    archives remain in memory and external document content is never fetched.

toolsPreview.name: summarize
toolsPreview.description:
EXTRACTIVE summarization, FAST and CPU-cheap — pull the most central (and, if
    you pass a `query`, most relevant) sentences straight out of a document, in their
    original order. No generative model, no hallucination: every returned sentence is
    verbatim from the input. Great for condensing scraped pages, long tool outputs,
    transcripts, or search snippets before you feed them to an LLM (cuts context/token
    cost). Method: embed each sentence with a small warm embedding model, score by
    centrality to the document centroid with MMR for diversity, return the top-k. Set
    `max_sentences` or `ratio`; add `query` for focused summaries. Returns {summary,
    sentences:[{index,text,score}], num_sentences}. Sub-second on a few-KB input.

toolsPreview.name: rag_search
toolsPreview.description:
Turnkey RETRIEVE for RAG, FAST — hand it a query and your documents and get back
    the most relevant passages, ranked, with scores + original indices. The one-call
    retrieval layer for agent RAG: embeds the query and passages with a small warm
    embedder (cosine top-N), then sharpens the shortlist with a warm cross-encoder
    reranker. Pass `documents` as a list of passages, or a single long string to have it
    sentence-chunked for you. Retrieval ONLY by default (your agent's LLM writes the
    final answer from the passages — keeps it fast and grounded); set `answer=true` to
    also synthesize an answer via the slow generative lane. Returns {results:[{index,
    text,score,rerank_score,embed_score}], reranked, models}. Sub-second for a few dozen
    short docs.

toolsPreview.name: submit_job
toolsPreview.description:
Submit a DURABLE bounded batch for asynchronous execution. The same principal +
    idempotency_key + body returns the same job while its bounded record is retained; reusing the
    retained key with a different body returns idempotency_conflict. Strict request/result-byte
    and per-principal/global job+item quotas apply. Only the published free-operation allowlist is accepted;
    paid x402/Stripe chat cannot be queued, so this tool cannot bypass payment gates. A signed
    OAuth or operator principal is required; shared demo/open principals cannot own jobs.

toolsPreview.name: get_job
toolsPreview.description:
Get principal-scoped job STATUS without returning stored inputs or results. States are
    queued, running, completed, failed, or cancelled; completed_items reports bounded progress.

toolsPreview.name: cancel_job
toolsPreview.description:
Cancel a job ONLY while it is still queued. Claim and cancellation are atomic, so once a
    worker has changed the state to running this returns job_not_cancellable and never interrupts
    in-flight model work. Repeating cancellation of an already-cancelled job is idempotent.

toolsPreview.name: get_job_result
toolsPreview.description:
Retrieve the bounded result of a principal-scoped terminal job. Each batch item has an
    independent succeeded/failed outcome with a machine-readable error. While queued/running,
    returns job_result_not_ready; results follow the advertised bounded retention policy.
